title: The startup capital and creation fee gating all Agent creation are left unspecified in the current Atlas
content:
The Agent lifecycle's entry condition is the deployment of startup capital and payment of a creation fee. Both are currently blank. A.2.2.3.1.1 on Capital Injection: "The required capital and the process for deploying it will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas." A.2.2.3.1.2 on the Creation Fee: "The required fee and the process for paying it will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas."

This leaves a structurally complete but unactuated gate. Everything downstream is fully specified — Proto-Agent creation, Scaffold Artifact setup, Founder Access assignment to the funding address, the ordered Primitive Invocation sequence — while the single precondition that admits anyone to that pipeline has no value.

It is worth recording because these two parameters carry most of the sybil- and quality-control weight in Agent formation. The Atlas's structural defences against frivolous Agents are thin by design; the capital and fee are where selectivity was meant to live. Until they are set, selectivity rests entirely on Core GovOps' validation that Founder documents are "well-specified" and "Aligned" (A.2.2.5.1.1.1.2) — a qualitative judgment rather than an economic filter.

The pattern matches the Founder Access suspension (A.2.2.1.1.3.2.1): the Atlas ships the full mechanism description with the not-yet-operational parts flagged in place, so specification and implementation state are read from the same document.
description: Both A.2.2.3.1.1 and A.2.2.3.1.2 defer amount and process to a future iteration, so the first gate in the Agent lifecycle has a defined role but no operative value.
